title: Cell-Penetrating Receptor Mimic Delivers a Long-Sought Blow Against Enteroviruses

analysis.time: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Cell-Penetrating Receptor Mimic Delivers a Long-Sought Blow Against Enteroviruses by October 13, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Cell-Penetrating Receptor Mimic Delivers a Long-Sought Blow Against Enteroviruses Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Hand, foot, and mouth disease is usually dismissed as a routine childhood illness, yet its most severe forms are caused by two closely related viruses that continue to claim young lives across Asia and beyond.
analysis.location_and_population: Not reported in the supplied evidence.
analysis.event: A research team led by Shijin Wang, Yubin Tang, and colleagues reports a molecule, RMP(R8), that mimics the human protein SCARB2, which is essential for enterovirus uncoating inside cells. The molecule shows promise in blocking EV-A71 and CV-A16 at low concentrations and improving survival in a neonatal mouse model.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The molecule demonstrated excellent safety and a wide therapeutic margin, with a half-maximal effective concentration of 0.156 micrograms per milliliter. It also showed activity across genetically divergent isolates of EV-A71 and CV-A16.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The molecule must still demonstrate an acceptable pharmacokinetic profile, stability against proteases, appropriate tissue distribution, and safety in larger animals. The dosing window in human infection will need careful definition.

analysis.brief_en: Researchers have developed a molecule, RMP(R8), that mimics the human protein SCARB2, which is crucial for enterovirus uncoating inside cells. This molecule effectively blocks EV-A71 and CV-A16 at low concentrations and improved survival in a neonatal mouse model. Further testing is needed to ensure its safety and efficacy in larger animals and humans.
analysis.summary_en: Researchers have developed a molecule, RMP(R8), that mimics the human protein SCARB2, which is crucial for enterovirus uncoating inside cells. This molecule effectively blocks EV-A71 and CV-A16 at low concentrations and improved survival in a neonatal mouse model. Further testing is needed to ensure its safety and efficacy in larger animals and humans.

analysis.location_and_population: The outbreaks are occurring in Hong Kong, primarily in child‐care centres, kindergartens and primary schools. Surveillance recorded eight outbreaks affecting 27 persons per week in mid‐September, and the recent nine outbreaks involved 24 persons, most of whom are children.
analysis.event: The Department of Health (DH) urged the public to maintain personal hygiene, and the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) issued letters to schools updating them on the rising HFMD activity. Surveillance data show eight outbreaks in mid‐September, increasing to 12, 11 and 20 outbreaks per week over the last three weeks, with nine outbreaks affecting 24 persons reported from Sunday to Tuesday.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Eight to twenty HFMD outbreaks have been recorded weekly, involving 24‐27 reported cases in the most recent periods. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: DH has issued a public hygiene reminder and CHP is sending letters to schools; institutions must report any outbreak immediately. Most cases occur in child‐care centres, kindergartens and primary schools, accounting for about 90% of outbreaks. DH has sent letters to schools and reminded the public that alcohol‐based hand rubs are not a substitute for soap and water. While surveillance continues, the data cover only institutional reports, so the broader community impact remains unclear.

analysis.time: The article was published on 15 Oct 2026 (07:40 pm) and reports a signing ceremony that took place on Thursday, 15 Oct 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The agreement covers distribution of the HFMD vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei. HFMD primarily affects children under five years of age.
analysis.event: Duopharma Biotech Bhd announced that its wholly‐owned unit Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd has secured exclusive rights to distribute Taiwan‐based Enimmune Corp's EnVAX‐A71 hand, foot and mouth disease vaccine in the three countries, subject to regulatory approval. The deal includes rights to market, sell and obtain marketing approval, and was confirmed by a company statement at the signing ceremony.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No case or death numbers are reported. HFMD is a contagious disease with frequent outbreaks in Malaysia and poses a significant public‐health risk, especially to children under five. The vaccine targets EV71, the strain linked to severe neurological complications.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Duopharma (M) is responsible for obtaining regulatory approval in each country; obligations terminate if approval is denied. The agreement remains in force for five years after launch, contingent on meeting minimum order quantities, and may be terminated if order thresholds are not met.

analysis.brief_en: Duopharma Biotech's wholly owned subsidiary, Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd, has signed an exclusive agreement with Taiwan's Enimmune Corp to distribute the EnVAX‐A71 hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei. The deal, announced on 15 October 2026, grants DMSB rights to market, sell and seek regulatory approval for the vaccine, which targets Enterovirus A71—a major cause of severe HFMD in children under five. While no case numbers are provided, HFMD remains a frequent public‐health concern in the region. Regulatory approval is pending in each country; if denied, DMSB's obligations end. The contract runs for five years post‐launch, subject to annual order minimums, and can be terminated for non‐compliance. This partnership aims to fill a vaccine gap for a disease that currently lacks an approved product in Malaysia.
analysis.summary_en: Duopharma Biotech's wholly owned subsidiary, Duopharma (M) Sdn Bhd, has signed an exclusive agreement with Taiwan's Enimmune Corp to distribute the EnVAX‐A71 hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) vaccine in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei. While no case numbers are provided, HFMD remains a frequent public‐health concern in the region. Regulatory approval is pending in each country; if denied, DMSB's obligations end. The contract runs for five years post‐launch, subject to annual order minimums, and can be terminated for non‐compliance. This partnership aims to fill a vaccine gap for a disease that currently lacks an approved product in Malaysia.
